fullPassage:
The Art of Dots

Have you ever zoomed in on a photo on your computer screen? If not, take a look at the image below.

When we look at the entire flower, it appears to have a gradual change in shade. Now, zoom in on the edge of the flower. You can see that it consists of many square dots with distinct colors and tones. Each tiny square dot is called a pixel.

Each pixel emits one of the three primary colors of light: red, green, or blue. Nonetheless, when viewing digital images, we can perceive secondary colors, such as yellow, cyan, and magenta, as well. These secondary colors are produced by putting primary colors next to each other. When equal amounts of red pixels and green pixels are put together, people perceive them as yellow. Likewise, people perceive the combination of blue and green pixels as cyan, and the combination of red and blue pixels as magenta. Take the yellow bell pepper on the screen as an example. We perceive the bell pepper as yellow, but if you look at it closely, there are a lot of red and green pixels next to each other.

The idea of using dots to produce another color is not new. Long before digital images were invented, French artists Georges Seurat and Paul Signac used a similar technique to paint their artworks in the 1880s. They were influenced by the color theory a French scientist had developed at the time. They did not use traditional brushstrokes to put paint on the canvas. Instead, they used tiny dots of individual colors to create an image. This technique is called Pointillism. The idea behind it is that when numerous dots of separate colors are placed next to each other, and then viewed from a distance, they blend in the viewer's eyes. Let's look at two examples of Pointillist style paintings.

This work named A Sunday Afternoon on the Island of La Grande Jatte was created by Georges Seurat, the pioneer of Pointillism. It portrays people looking at the river, reading books, or sitting on the grass. We can see some animals including a dog and a monkey as well. The grass on which the shade falls is painted dark. However, other areas without shadow are painted bright. This sharp contrast is pretty impressive. This work is a representative work of Pointillism. It is mostly painted with dots instead of dashes or lines. If you look closer, you will notice that there are no object boundary lines. It also has multiple distinct colors of dots to represent a single color, which adds more vibrancy to the painting.

Take a look at a part of the monkey from the original picture. Its body is made up of a variety of different colored dots. However, when viewed from a distance, the dots of various colors optically merge to produce brown. In the process of creating this work, Seurat kept studying color composition, analyzing it, and revising this work. It took him two years to produce this huge piece because he arranged every single dot with purpose and intention. Since he created art using color theory, Seurat is known as a scientific artist. He himself also said, "Some say they see poetry in my paintings; I see only science."

Now, let's look at another Pointillist painting, Women at the Well, painted in 1892 by Paul Signac, a contemporary of Seurat.

In this work, two individuals are drawing water from a well with a container. Behind the women are a lighthouse and boats in the ocean. This artwork portrays a hot sunny day in southern France through the contrast of yellow sand and blue ocean. Upon closer inspection, all the objects in the picture are composed of small dots. It is worth noting that Signac did not simply paint the grass green by combining yellow and blue. Rather, he placed separate dots of yellow, blue, and green next to each other. Viewers then perceive the combination of these colors as green. Signac changed the proportions of these colors to create the various shades of green.

The era of Pointillism came to an end after the first half of the twentieth century. However, this new and scientific method of painting had a great influence on later art groups. Modern artists have adopted the basic concept of dots and applied it to their works in a variety of shapes and forms.

questions.passage: Each pixel emits one of the three primary colors of light: red, green, or blue. Nonetheless, when ①<u>viewing</u> digital images, we can perceive secondary colors, such as yellow, cyan, and magenta, as well. questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.korean: ④ for → as (perceive A as B: A를 B로 인식하다)
det.analysis:
① viewing: 분사구문(= when we are viewing). 주어 일치 — 적절

② produced: 수동태(be produced by ~). 이차색은 일차색에 의해 만들어짐 — 적절

③ as: perceive A as B 구문. 사람들은 그것을 노란색으로 인식 — 적절

④ for → as: perceive A as B가 올바른 구문. for는 perceive와 함께 쓰이지 않음 ← 정답
det.tip: perceive A as B = A를 B로 인식하다. for가 아닌 as가 올바른 전치사.

questions.passage: The idea of using dots to produce another color is not new. They were ①<u>influenced</u> by the color theory a French scientist had developed at the time. They did not use traditional brushstrokes to put paint on the canvas. Instead, they used tiny dots of individual colors ②<u>to create</u> an image. This technique is called Pointillism. The idea behind it is that when numerous dots of separate colors are ③<u>placing</u> next to each other, and then viewed from a distance, they ④<u>blend</u> in the viewer's eyes.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.korean: ③ placing → placed (수동태: are placed next to each other)
det.analysis:
① influenced: be influenced by ~ (수동태). 색채이론의 영향을 받았다 — 적절

② to create: 목적의 to부정사. 이미지를 만들기 위해 점을 사용했다 — 적절

③ placing → placed: 'when dots are placed'에서 수동태(be + p.p.)가 필요. 점들이 놓여지는 것이므로 능동형 placing은 부적절 ← 정답

④ blend: 주어 they(= dots)가 섞이다. 능동 의미로 적절 — 적절
det.tip: dots are placed(놓여지다) = 수동태. are placing은 능동이므로 의미 불일치.

questions.passage: This work named A Sunday Afternoon on the Island of La Grande Jatte was created by Georges Seurat, the pioneer of Pointillism. It portrays people looking at the river, reading books, or sitting on the grass. We can see some animals ①<u>including</u> a dog and a monkey as well. The grass on which the shade falls is painted dark. This work is a representative work of Pointillism. It is mostly painted with dots instead of dashes or lines. It also has multiple distinct colors of dots to represent a single color, ②<u>which</u> adds more vibrancy to the painting. In the process of creating this work, Seurat kept ③<u>studying</u> color composition, analyzing it, and revising this work. It took him two years to produce this huge piece because he arranged every single dot with purpose and ④<u>intend</u>.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.korean: ④ intend → intention (전치사 with 뒤에 명사 필요, purpose and intention 병렬)
det.analysis:
① including: 전치사적 분사. '~를 포함하여'의 의미로 a dog and a monkey 수식 — 적절

② which: 계속적 용법의 관계대명사(, which). 앞 절 전체를 선행사로 받아 '그것이 더 많은 활기를 더한다' — 적절

③ studying: keep + V-ing (동명사 목적어). studying, analyzing, revising 병렬 — 적절

④ intend → intention: with purpose and ___에서 purpose(명사)와 and로 병렬되므로 명사 intention이 필요. 동사원형 intend는 부적절 ← 정답
det.tip: purpose and intention — 등위접속사 and로 연결된 명사 병렬 구조. 동사 intend가 아닌 명사 intention이 필요.

questions.passage: When we look at the entire flower, it appears to have a gradual change in shade. Now, zoom in on the edge of the flower. You can see that it consists of many square dots with ①<u>distinct</u> colors and tones. Each tiny square dot is called a pixel. Each pixel emits one of the three primary colors of light: red, green, or blue. Nonetheless, when viewing digital images, we can perceive ②<u>secondary</u> colors, such as yellow, cyan, and magenta, as well. These secondary colors are produced by putting primary colors next to each other. When ③<u>unequal</u> amounts of red pixels and green pixels are put together, people perceive them as yellow. Likewise, people perceive the combination of blue and green pixels as cyan, and the combination of red and blue pixels as ④<u>magenta</u>.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.korean: ③ unequal → equal (같은 양의 빨강·초록 픽셀을 합치면 노란색으로 인식)
det.analysis:
① distinct (뚜렷한): 각 사각형 점이 뚜렷한 색과 톤을 갖는다 — 원문 그대로 적절

② secondary (이차적인): 이차색(노랑, 시안, 마젠타)을 인지한다 — 원문 그대로 적절

③ unequal (불균등한) → equal (균등한): 원문은 'equal amounts of red pixels and green pixels'로 같은 양의 빨강·초록 픽셀을 합쳐야 노란색으로 보인다는 내용 ← 정답

④ magenta (마젠타): 빨강+파랑 = 마젠타 — 원문 그대로 적절
det.tip: equal amounts = 같은 양. unequal은 반의어로 문맥에 부적절.

questions.passage: This work named A Sunday Afternoon on the Island of La Grande Jatte was created by Georges Seurat, the ①<u>pioneer</u> of Pointillism. It portrays people looking at the river, reading books, or sitting on the grass. The grass on which the shade falls is painted dark. However, other areas without shadow are painted bright. This sharp contrast is pretty ②<u>impressive</u>. It is mostly painted with dots instead of dashes or lines. It also has multiple distinct colors of dots to represent a single color, which adds more ③<u>monotony</u> to the painting. In the process of creating this work, Seurat kept studying color composition, analyzing it, and revising this work. It took him two years to produce this huge piece because he arranged every single dot with purpose and ④<u>intention</u>.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.korean: ③ monotony(단조로움) → vibrancy(활기, 생동감)
det.analysis:
① pioneer (선구자): 쇠라가 점묘법의 선구자라는 설명 — 원문 그대로 적절

② impressive (인상적인): 밝음과 어둠의 대비가 매우 인상적이라는 내용 — 원문 그대로 적절

③ monotony (단조로움) → vibrancy (활기): 원문은 'adds more vibrancy to the painting'으로 다양한 색의 점이 그림에 생동감을 더한다는 의미. monotony는 반의어 ← 정답

④ intention (의도): 쇠라가 모든 점을 목적과 의도를 갖고 배치했다 — 원문 그대로 적절
det.tip: vibrancy = 활기, 생동감. monotony = 단조로움. 다채로운 색 점이 그림에 더하는 것은 생동감이지 단조로움이 아님.

questions.passage: The idea of using dots to produce another color is not new. Long before digital images were invented, French artists Georges Seurat and Paul Signac used a similar technique to paint their artworks in the 1880s. They were influenced by the color theory a French scientist had developed at the time. They did not use traditional brushstrokes to put paint on the canvas. Instead, they used tiny dots of individual colors to create an image. This technique is called Pointillism. The idea behind it is that when numerous dots of separate colors are placed next to each other, and then __________, they blend in the viewer's eyes.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 멀리서 바라보면 (viewed from a distance)
det.analysis:
① viewed from a distance (멀리서 바라보면): 점묘법의 핵심 원리. 분리된 색의 점들이 나란히 놓이고 멀리서 보면 보는 이의 눈에서 혼합된다 ← 정답
→ 본문: "viewed from a distance, they blend in the viewer's eyes"

② painted on a canvas (캔버스에 칠하면): 캔버스에 칠하는 것은 과정이지 혼합 조건이 아님

③ mixed with a brush (붓으로 섞으면): 점묘법은 전통적 붓 기법을 사용하지 않는다고 명시됨

④ analyzed under a microscope (현미경으로 분석하면): 본문 내용과 무관한 과학적 분석 맥락
det.tip: 점묘법의 핵심: 멀리서 보면(from a distance) 개별 점들이 하나의 색으로 혼합되어 보인다.

questions.passage: It is worth noting that Signac did not simply paint the grass green by combining yellow and blue. Rather, he placed separate dots of yellow, blue, and green next to each other. Viewers then perceive the combination of these colors as green. Signac changed __________ to create the various shades of green. The era of Pointillism came to an end after the first half of the twentieth century. However, this new and scientific method of painting had a great influence on later art groups.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 이 색들의 비율 (the proportions of these colors)
det.analysis:
① the proportions of these colors (이 색들의 비율): 시냑이 노랑, 파랑, 초록의 비율을 조절하여 다양한 녹색 음영을 만들었다 ← 정답
→ 본문: "Signac changed the proportions of these colors to create the various shades of green"

② the shapes of individual dots (개별 점의 형태): 점의 형태 변화는 본문에서 언급되지 않음

③ the number of brush strokes (붓 터치 횟수): 점묘법은 전통적 붓 터치를 쓰지 않음

④ the surface of the canvas (캔버스 표면): 캔버스 표면 변경은 본문과 무관
det.tip: proportion = 비율. 색의 비율을 조절하여 다양한 음영(shade)을 만드는 것이 점묘법의 기법.

questions.passage: Each pixel emits one of the three primary colors of light: red, green, or blue. Nonetheless, when viewing digital images, we can perceive secondary colors, such as yellow, cyan, and magenta, as well. These secondary colors are produced by putting primary colors next to each other. When equal amounts of red pixels and green pixels are put together, people perceive them as yellow. questions.stem: 다음 글의 내용과 일치하는 것은?
ch: 각 픽셀은 세 가지 이차색 중 하나를 발산한다.
빨강과 파랑 픽셀의 조합은 시안으로 인식된다.
노란색을 만들기 위해서는 파랑과 초록 픽셀이 필요하다.

det.korean: 이차색은 일차색을 나란히 배치하여 만들어진다
det.analysis:
① 각 픽셀은 세 가지 이차색 중 하나를 발산한다: 일차색(primary colors)을 발산함. 이차색(secondary)이 아님

② 이차색은 일차색을 나란히 배치하여 만들어진다: "produced by putting primary colors next to each other" 원문 일치 ← 정답

③ 빨강과 파랑 픽셀의 조합은 시안으로 인식된다: 빨강+파랑 = 마젠타(magenta). 시안은 파랑+초록

④ 노란색을 만들기 위해서는 파랑과 초록 픽셀이 필요하다: 노란색 = 빨강 + 초록. 파랑 + 초록 = 시안
det.tip: secondary colors are produced by putting primary colors next to each other.

questions.stem: 다음 글의 내용과 일치하지 않는 것은?
ch: 쇠라의 작품에는 강을 바라보는 사람들이 묘사되어 있다.
그림 속 그늘이 드리운 잔디는 어둡게 칠해져 있다.
가까이 보면 물체의 경계선이 없다는 것을 알 수 있다.
이 작품은 주로 선과 대시를 사용하여 그려졌다.

det.korean: 이 작품은 주로 선과 대시가 아닌 점으로 그려졌다
det.analysis:
① 쇠라의 작품에는 강을 바라보는 사람들이 묘사되어 있다: "portrays people looking at the river" 일치

② 그림 속 그늘이 드리운 잔디는 어둡게 칠해져 있다: "The grass on which the shade falls is painted dark" 일치

③ 가까이 보면 물체의 경계선이 없다는 것을 알 수 있다: "no object boundary lines" 일치

④ 이 작품은 주로 선과 대시를 사용하여 그려졌다: 원문은 "mostly painted with dots instead of dashes or lines" — 점으로 그려졌지 선이 아님 ← 정답
det.tip: dots instead of dashes or lines = 대시나 선이 아닌 점으로.

questions.stem: 다음 글의 내용과 일치하지 않는 것은?
ch: 시냑의 작품에서 두 사람이 우물에서 물을 긷고 있다.
여인들 뒤에 등대와 바다 위의 배가 보인다.
시냑은 노랑과 파랑만 섞어서 잔디를 초록으로 칠했다.
시냑은 색의 비율을 조절하여 다양한 녹색 음영을 만들었다.

det.korean: 시냑은 노랑과 파랑만 섞어 칠한 것이 아니라 노랑, 파랑, 초록 점을 각각 나란히 배치했다
det.analysis:
① 시냑의 작품에서 두 사람이 우물에서 물을 긷고 있다: "two individuals are drawing water from a well" 일치

② 여인들 뒤에 등대와 바다 위의 배가 보인다: "Behind the women are a lighthouse and boats in the ocean" 일치

③ 시냑은 노랑과 파랑만 섞어서 잔디를 초록으로 칠했다: 원문은 "did not simply paint the grass green by combining yellow and blue. Rather, he placed separate dots of yellow, blue, and green next to each other" — 단순히 섞지 않고 분리된 점을 나란히 배치 ← 정답

④ 시냑은 색의 비율을 조절하여 다양한 녹색 음영을 만들었다: "changed the proportions of these colors to create the various shades of green" 일치
det.tip: Signac did NOT simply combine — he placed separate dots. 핵심은 '섞은 것'이 아니라 '분리된 점 배치'.

questions.passage: Each pixel emits one of the three primary colors of light: red, green, or blue. Nonetheless, when viewing digital images, we can perceive secondary colors, such as yellow, cyan, and magenta, as well. These secondary colors are produced by putting primary colors next to each other. When equal amounts of red pixels and green pixels are put together, people perceive them as yellow. Likewise, people perceive the combination of blue and green pixels as cyan, and the combination of red and blue pixels as magenta. Take the yellow bell pepper on the screen as an example. We perceive the bell pepper as yellow, but if you look at it closely, there are a lot of red and green pixels next to each other.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 주제로 가장 적절한 것은?
ch: the history of pixel technology in modern screens
the invention of digital imaging software
the difference between primary and secondary colors in art
the principle of producing secondary colors from pixels

det.korean: 픽셀에서 이차색이 만들어지는 원리
det.analysis:
① the history of pixel technology in modern screens (현대 화면의 픽셀 기술 역사): 역사에 대한 설명이 아님

② the invention of digital imaging software (디지털 이미징 소프트웨어의 발명): 소프트웨어 발명 내용 없음

③ the difference between primary and secondary colors in art (미술에서 일차색과 이차색의 차이): 미술이 아닌 디지털 이미지에 대한 내용

④ the principle of producing secondary colors from pixels (픽셀에서 이차색이 만들어지는 원리): 일차색 픽셀을 나란히 놓으면 이차색으로 인식되는 원리를 설명하는 본문 내용과 정확히 일치 ← 정답
det.tip: 핵심: 일차색 픽셀의 나란한 배치 → 이차색 인식이라는 원리.

questions.passage: The idea of using dots to produce another color is not new. Long before digital images were invented, French artists Georges Seurat and Paul Signac used a similar technique to paint their artworks in the 1880s. They were influenced by the color theory a French scientist had developed at the time. They did not use traditional brushstrokes to put paint on the canvas. Instead, they used tiny dots of individual colors to create an image. This technique is called Pointillism. The era of Pointillism came to an end after the first half of the twentieth century. However, this new and scientific method of painting had a great influence on later art groups. Modern artists have adopted the basic concept of dots and applied it to their works in a variety of shapes and forms.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 주제로 가장 적절한 것은?
ch: the connection between scientific color theory and Pointillism's lasting artistic legacy
the rivalry between Seurat and Signac in developing Pointillism
the decline of traditional painting techniques in the twentieth century
the superiority of digital art over Pointillist techniques

det.korean: 과학적 색채 이론과 점묘법의 지속적인 예술적 유산 사이의 관계
det.analysis:
① the connection between scientific color theory and Pointillism's lasting artistic legacy (과학적 색채 이론과 점묘법의 지속적인 예술적 유산 사이의 관계): 프랑스 과학자의 색채 이론 → 점묘법 탄생 → 20세기 이후에도 현대 미술에 영향이라는 흐름과 일치 ← 정답

② the rivalry between Seurat and Signac in developing Pointillism (쇠라와 시냑의 경쟁): 두 화가의 경쟁은 본문에 없음. 둘은 동시대인(contemporary)

③ the decline of traditional painting techniques in the twentieth century (20세기 전통 회화 기법의 쇠퇴): 전통 기법의 쇠퇴가 주제가 아님

④ the superiority of digital art over Pointillist techniques (점묘법 대비 디지털 아트의 우월성): 우열 비교는 본문에 없음
det.tip: 색채 이론의 영향 → 점묘법 탄생 → 후대 미술에 영향. 과학과 예술의 연결이 핵심.

questions.passage: Take a look at a part of the monkey from the original picture. Its body is made up of a variety of different colored dots. However, when viewed from a distance, the dots of various colors optically merge to produce brown. In the process of creating this work, Seurat kept studying color composition, analyzing it, and revising this work. It took him two years to produce this huge piece because he arranged every single dot with purpose and intention. Since he created art using color theory, Seurat is known as a scientific artist. He himself also said, <u>"Some say they see poetry in my paintings; I see only science."</u>

Seurat believed that scientific knowledge was more valuable than artistic talent.

det.korean: 쇠라의 예술은 감정적 표현보다 계산된 과학적 원리에 기반했다
det.analysis:
① Seurat's art was based on calculated scientific principles rather than emotional expression (쇠라의 예술은 감정적 표현보다 계산된 과학적 원리에 기반했다): 다른 사람들은 그의 그림에서 시(감성)를 보지만 자신은 오직 과학만 본다는 말은, 그가 감성이 아닌 과학적 원리를 토대로 예술을 했다는 의미 ← 정답
→ 본문: "he arranged every single dot with purpose and intention" + "created art using color theory"

② Seurat believed that scientific knowledge was more valuable than artistic talent (쇠라는 과학 지식이 예술적 재능보다 더 가치있다고 믿었다): 과학과 예술의 가치 비교가 아니라 자신의 작업 방식에 대한 언급

③ Seurat's paintings were considered unartistic by most art critics of his time (쇠라의 그림은 당시 대부분의 비평가에게 비예술적이라 여겨졌다): 비평가 평가에 대한 내용 없음

④ Seurat preferred writing poetry to painting with colors on canvas (쇠라는 캔버스에 그리는 것보다 시 쓰기를 선호했다): poetry는 비유적 표현이지 실제 시 쓰기가 아님
det.tip: poetry = 감성/예술성, science = 계산/원리. 쇠라는 자신의 작업이 과학적 계산에 기반한다고 자부했다.

questions.passage: This artwork portrays a hot sunny day in southern France through the contrast of yellow sand and blue ocean. Upon closer inspection, all the objects in the picture are composed of small dots. It is worth noting that Signac did not simply paint the grass green by combining yellow and blue. Rather, he placed separate dots of yellow, blue, and green next to each other. Viewers then perceive the combination of these colors as green. Signac changed the proportions of these colors to create the various shades of green.
